test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Fly off the handle

options.text: To lose one’s temper suddenly and unexpectedly
To make a mistake while performing a task

solution:
The correct answer is "**To lose one's temper suddenly and unexpectedly.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **"Fly off the handle" is an idiom that means to suddenly lose one's temper**.

 
 
• Example: When Jack's father found out about the incidence, he really flew off the handle.
 
 
 
• The phrase likely comes from the idea of a tool or weapon flying out of someone's hand when they lose control of it.
 
• Other synonyms for this idiom include "blow up," "go ballistic," and "lose it."
 
• Thus, it is clear that option 2 explains the given idiom correctly.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.
